title: Smooth marginal densities for finitely delayed Brownian equations under the uniform strong endpoint Hörmander condition
author: Reda Chhaibi; Ibrahim Ekren
work: A Hörmander condition for delayed stochastic differential equations
source_version: Annales Henri Lebesgue 3 (2020), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/ahl.53
difficulty_reason: The authored proof enhances Brownian motion and its delays into a geometric rough path, factors Malliavin derivatives on the final delay-free interval, and propagates covariance smallness through endpoint Lie brackets using quantitative rough Norris estimates. This non-Markovian smoothing construction exceeds qualifying examinations.

primary_locator.selected_hypotheses: analytic Assumption1.1 and uniform strong endpoint geometric Assumption1.4(1)
primary_locator.required_core: complete shifted Brownian lift, delayed derivative/factorization, inverse-flow and rough bracket/Norris arguments

source_scope_note: The selected problem is Theorem 1.5 under analytic Assumption 1.1 and uniform strong endpoint Hormander Assumption 1.4(1) only, with the exact finite deterministic delays, constant prehistory, bounded smooth derivatives and Stratonovich Lipschitz hypotheses. The complete author body retains all local shifted-Brownian rough lift, small-ball, delayed Malliavin factorization, final-interval inverse-flow, endpoint bracket and quantitative Norris arguments. Weak semi-bracket and bounded pointwise alternatives and examples are unselected context.
